key_insight: Search scaling improves autonomous research performance in factor mining, with stronger models starting better but deeper search narrowing the gap and broader parallel search working best.
engineering_relevance: For agentic research systems, where and how test-time computation is spent matters: adaptive search policies and parallel exploration can improve final scientific outputs without changing the underlying model.
method: Evaluated 50 quantitative factor-mining tasks from financial research reports.
Compared nine LLMs across different search budgets, search depths, and search organizations.
Transferred intermediate research states between models and contrasted parallel vs. sequential search strategies.
evidence_signal: The study traces end-to-end research trajectories across 50 tasks and 9 models, using budgeted search and intermediate-state transfer to measure how search design affects factor quality.
watch_item: Results are task-specific to financial factor mining, so gains may not transfer directly to other scientific discovery settings or to deployments with tighter compute and latency limits.
paper_title: From Search to Research: Exploring Search Scaling in Autonomous Quantitative Factor Mining
